site.name: GTA VI PC Tracker
site.description: Live standings of the unofficial projects trying to run the Xbox build of GTA VI on a PC: how far each has got, what changed, and a best guess at when it becomes playable.

headline_note: No project is confirmed playable yet. Vice-Tay's README reports a median of 21.1 frames a second over a 30-minute session by hand on an RTX 4090, but one session, self-reported, and it does not say how the session ended. AnyXboxX reports a median of about 24 over a 14-minute session on an RTX 4070 SUPER, also self-reported. KLBF Lab reports an average of 14 over 37 minutes so far and 77 minutes on an earlier build; VIctory-7900XTX reports about 16 to 20 in short runs. Playable needs 20 for 30 minutes without a crash.

stages.name: Loads
stages.bar: The game's executable loads with its imports resolved.

stages.name: Starts up
stages.bar: The game's own start-up code runs: memory, threads, archives.

stages.name: Graphics device
stages.bar: The game creates its graphics device and queues on the PC.

stages.name: First frames
stages.bar: Frames are presented to a window, even if they are black.

stages.name: Recognisable picture
stages.bar: The game's own screens can be seen: logos, menus, video or setup pages.

stages.name: In-game
stages.bar: The game world is loaded and running, with or without a usable picture.

stages.name: Playable
stages.bar: 30 minutes or more in the world under player control, at 20 frames a second or better, without a crash.

projects.name: Vice-Tay
projects.tagline: VIctory tree tuned and fixed on one RTX 4090 PC, built on VIctory, victory-fork, VIctory-7900XTX and other forks
projects.furthest: The prologue through the boat section to an island, 30 minutes in the world by hand at a median of 21.1 fps (self-reported)
projects.status: Its README (27 Nov) still reports the 30-minute session played by hand on the Series S profile, from the prison through cutscenes and the boat section to an island, with the HUD, minimap and pause menu working. The median was 21.1 fps (1% low 17.0) on one RTX 4090, with a median frame time of 47.3 ms. It does not say how the session ended, and it is one session, so this page keeps the project at stage 6 even though speed and length reach the bar's numbers. It adds a 6-minute test on an experimental build with 2x frame generation: 22.4 rendered and 44.9 presented fps. The README lists faults: colour banding, flat-colour surfaces, blocky clouds and reflections, and ray-traced light only with a switch. Memory peaked at 24.1 GB in the playtest, and the README says the 30 fps target is not met. It also reports that an RX 6700 XT on Windows 11 LTSC can reset the device while loading the world.
projects.source: project README (27 Nov) and commits to 6594538; one RTX 4090 and Ryzen 9 9950X3D, self-reported

picture.note: lit; colour banding, glowing objects, block-edged clouds and missing ray-traced light; shade not described

speed.note: median 21.1 over 30 minutes on the Series S profile; 19.1 to 23.2 for the middle 80%

stability.note: 30 minutes in the world by hand; the README does not say how the session ended

projects.name: AnyXboxX
projects.tagline: Xbox Series emulator focused on this one game, built on Vice-Tay
projects.furthest: The open world at a median of about 24 fps in Full HD over a 14-minute session on an RTX 4070 SUPER (maintainer's measurement)
projects.status: Its README (status dated 27 Nov) now reports a 14-minute launcher session in the world at a median of about 24 fps at 1920 by 1080 with the Series X profile on an RTX 4070 SUPER and i7-13700KF, with the game's own 30 fps cap held in scenes up to about 4,000 draws, and about 20 fps at 4K. Heavy scenes of 7,000 to 11,000 draws still fall to 10 to 18 fps. The gain follows moving its VIctory copy onto Vice-Tay's code and giving the worker threads more room on CPUs with 16 or more logical cores (19.6 to 23.8 fps median in one pair of runs, commit f99cbee). Ray tracing is off, so indoor and shadowed areas are dark, and the game uses 20 to 25 GB of RAM. The README does not say how the 14-minute session ended. The project says it is focused on NVIDIA and that AMD cards work less well.
projects.source: project README (status dated 27 Nov) and commits to 0eea573, including f99cbee and e6701c0; maintainer's RTX 4070 SUPER, self-reported

picture.note: lit, with an ambient stand-in for ray-traced light; shade dark with ray tracing off

speed.note: median 24.4 in the world at 1080p; about 20 at 4K; heavy scenes 10 to 18

stability.note: 14-minute launcher session; the README does not say how it ended

projects.name: KLBF Lab
projects.tagline: VIctory and victory-fork build with its own fixes, tested first on an AMD card; repository opened 25 Nov
projects.furthest: Free roam after the first mission, at an average of 14 fps over 37 minutes so far on a test build (self-reported)
projects.status: Its README (26 Nov) reports test build Lab 61, on a separate beta-2 branch, measured in ordinary play on one RX 9070 XT with a controller, the Series S profile and upscaling. A session still running at 37 minutes without a crash averaged 14.0 fps, median 14.5, with 16% of the time at 18 fps or more and 6% under 5 fps in freezes. Peaks run from 27 fps looking at the sky to 12 to 17 in traffic and driving. Water surfaces and car glass are not drawn and mirrors are black. The longest finished session it states is 77 minutes on the earlier test build Lab 39, ended by the testers, not a crash, which reached free roam after the first mission. Those two results come from different builds, and the 20 fps bar is not met. The README also points to a newer test build, Lab 63, which it says fixes dark faces in shade, and to a shared 5-minute test. Its latest-run line (26 Nov) now gives 16.3 fps average (1% low 6.2, 4 freezes) for a new AMD beta branch on the same card in that 5-minute test; this page keeps the longer Lab 61 figures for the lanes.
projects.source: project README (26 Nov, Lab 61 on beta-2, with Lab 35 and Lab 39 results and the AMD beta latest-run line) and its latest commits; one RX 9070 XT, self-reported; the 37-minute session was still running when the README was written

picture.note: lit; water and car glass not drawn, mirrors black

speed.note: average 14.0, median 14.5 over 37 minutes on Lab 61

stability.note: 77 minutes on Lab 39, ended by choice; Lab 61 is at 37 minutes so far

projects.name: victory-fork
projects.tagline: Fork of VIctory aimed at a correct, playable picture
projects.furthest: The open world and the first boat mission at 8 to 14 fps, in sessions of up to 49 minutes that end in a device loss
projects.status: Its README (status of 27 Nov, 06:30 UTC) says the tester played from the opening through the prologue and past the first boat mission, at about 11 fps at the first boat mission (8.5 in heavier views) on one RTX 4070 with the Series X profile; the thread preparing submissions, not the card, is the limit. The graphics card is still lost 30 to 50 minutes into a session, with a 49-minute and a 38-minute run ending that way and a hang after 6 minutes. The cause is not known. New on 27 Nov: with the ray-tracing structure builder on, which is the default, ray-traced shadows and light show once a scene has streamed in, but the frame rate falls to about 0.2 to 3 fps; with the builder off, anything the sun does not hit is black. Open water now shows waves with no black patches.
projects.source: the fork's own README (status header of 27 Nov, 06:30 UTC) and its commits; one RTX 4070, self-reported

picture.note: sunlit, out of the sun black at the usual speed; ray-traced shade shows only with the builder on, at 0.2 to 3 fps

speed.note: about 11 fps at the first boat mission, 8.5 in heavier views (builder off)

stability.note: 49 minutes, ended by a device loss

projects.name: Kelvaroq
projects.tagline: Rust-based Xbox Series runtime for Windows built on VIctory and victory-fork; repository opened 24 Nov
projects.furthest: The prologue and first mission, 36 minutes without a crash at about 10 fps (outside tester)
projects.status: Its README (25 Nov) says the prologue runs at about 10 fps in typical views and 7 to 8 in the heaviest scenes, on one RTX 5080 at 3840 by 2160, with menus, character control, HUD and pause verified in play. It also reports an outside tester's monitored session on an RTX 4090 at 2560 by 1440: 36 min 46 s without a crash, mean 10 fps, median 11, range 1 to 20, and 9 to 12 after the first 10 minutes. That session covered the prologue and the first mission and is one session only. The README says about 7% of draws are still dropped, mostly because ray-tracing structures are not built, and that the thread preparing GPU work limits heavy frames. Its badge calls the project playable; this page's bar is 20 fps, which is not met. The README does not describe the picture, so that lane is empty. Its README (26 Nov) adds that a new memory layer and native ray tracing work in a build under test that is not public, and says the first scenes copy under 8 MB a frame instead of over 100 MB; it gives no frame rate for that build, so the lanes still use the public build. The repository has moved to a studio's organisation.
projects.source: project README (26 Nov) and commits to e062a82; developer's RTX 5080 and an outside tester's RTX 4090, self-reported; the memory layer and ray tracing are claims about a private test build

speed.note: 7 to 12 fps; about 10 in typical views

stability.note: 36 min 46 s by an outside tester, no crash

projects.name: darkworldhm's stream build
projects.tagline: Private build shown on a Rumble stream, reportedly based on VIctory. No public code
projects.furthest: Free roam at about 12 to 15 fps, as far into the story as the leading builds (unconfirmed)
projects.status: A build shown on darkworldhm's Rumble stream on 25 Nov is reported to run free roam at about 12 to 15 fps, swinging between 5 and 24, with no crash so far. The picture is said to look acceptable with some texture or ray-tracing glitches. The card is reportedly an NVIDIA RTX 50-series. It is said to be built on VIctory, but which fork is not known. This page has not seen the stream and no code is public, so every figure is second-hand and unconfirmed. No session length is given, so the stability lane is empty and it ranks below victory-fork.

projects.name: VIctory-Belobug-AMD
projects.tagline: AMD Radeon fork of VIctory, created 25 Nov
projects.furthest: A city street at about 19 fps on the Series X profile with two renderer patches, in a README written for an RX 7900 XTX
projects.status: Its README (status dated 26 Nov) is titled for an RX 7900 XTX and gives one scene, a city street, on an i9-12900K with ray tracing off: about 45 ms a frame (about 22 fps) on the Series S profile with five optional patches, about 53 ms (about 19 fps) on the Series X profile with two, and 57 to 75 ms (13 to 17 fps) without the patches. It is the older text of VIctory-7900XTX, so the figures may come from that machine, not from this repository's maintainer. The 41-minute session and the street-chase figures are no longer in the README, so the stability lane is empty. Newer commits port an FSR 4.1.2 upscale to 4K from DexNom's fork (cd8dfc0) and upload title textures earlier in each submission to fix frame order and flicker (5d6bd84). The README states that rooms with little light are not yet right. This page takes 19 fps.

projects.name: VIctory-7900XTX
projects.tagline: VIctory and victory-fork build tuned for speed on an AMD RX 7900 XTX; created 25 Nov
projects.furthest: A city street at about 16 to 20 fps on the Series X profile with ray tracing off, 9 to 10 with it on
projects.status: Its README (status dated 26 Nov) was rewritten again and now gives 270-second runs in one city street on one machine, with five optional renderer patches on. On the Series X profile at 1440p drawn to 4K with ray tracing off it gives 49 ms a frame standing (20 fps) and about 62 ms walking (16 fps); with ray tracing on, the stated goal, 99 ms standing (10 fps) and about 110 ms walking (9 fps). The Series S profile gives 23 fps standing and 16 walking. It uses about 37 to 45 GB of memory and recommends 64 GB of RAM. It says trees and lighting were fixed on 26 Nov, but models and textures stay at low detail for a long time while streaming and some ray-traced structures of moving objects are corrupt. It states no session length, so the stability lane is empty. This page takes the Series X figures with ray tracing off, 18 fps as the midpoint.
projects.source: project README (status dated 26 Nov, rewritten again since the last check) and commits to the renderer-port-7 commit; one i9-12900K and RX 7900 XTX, self-reported; frame times converted to fps by this page

projects.name: XCL
projects.tagline: General Xbox Series to Windows compatibility layer, in the spirit of Proton
projects.furthest: Its 3D world at about 5 fps, on an unmerged integration branch (picture incomplete)
projects.status: The README says the game starts in about 4 seconds and holds 30 fps in its menus. With an NVIDIA integration branch, a draft pull request that is not meant to be merged, it goes on into its 3D world at about 5 fps on an RTX 5090. The README says the world's picture is incomplete, some mesh pipelines are refused and it does not keep running there for long. It rates the game at about 60% of the way to playable, an estimate. All 26,698 of the game's GPU programs translate.

projects.name: VItoriaBr
projects.tagline: Portuguese-language continuation of VIctory with victory-fork's fixes, tested on NVIDIA
projects.furthest: The open world, lit by depth bounds, at up to 6 fps
projects.status: Its README (25 Nov) says the game loads into the world and renders the opening cutscene, the first room and the open world, with water, vehicles, a HUD and subtitles, at up to 6 fps on an RTX 5060 Ti (3.5 to 6 with its recommended settings), without a driver reset. Shade is filled by an ambient light worked out from depth, not by the game's ray tracing. It also warns that entering the world on a real card can still reset the display driver. It names no mission and no play time. A section added on 26 Nov reports 4 to 6 fps for the current main preset and 22 fps for an experimental build of its own that is not in the preset; this page does not use the 22 fps figure, which is unreleased and self-reported. The same section says the author rates stability as occasional crashes.
projects.source: project README (26 Nov, evidence section) and commits to 1361e19; one RTX 5060 Ti, self-reported

projects.name: ScarlettPort
projects.tagline: Packages VIctory and XCL with its own fixes and launcher; started 24 Nov
projects.furthest: Control in the opening area with a fuller lit picture, at about 3 fps
projects.status: Its README (27 Nov, versions 0.5.0 to 0.5.2, progress 90%) says the game reaches player control in the opening area with a full lit picture without ray tracing. Its own measurement is 3.4 fps in the world on an RTX 3060 with the Series S profile (v0.5.0), up from 1.6, and the world loads in 178 s. It says no long run has been recorded, so stability is unmeasured, and that NVIDIA cards are still slow at 3 to 6 fps. Its list of community reports, which the README says are not its own measurements, includes 22.0 fps median on an RX 9060 XT with version 0.5.2 and 13.4 fps average on an RTX 4070 Ti with 0.5.1. This page treats those as second-hand and does not use them for the lanes.

projects.name: VIctory
projects.tagline: Runs the game's Xbox code natively on Windows
projects.furthest: The prologue, fully drawn, at about 1 fps
projects.status: The upstream code base most stage-6 projects build on. Its README (25 Nov) says the game boots, runs its menus at 30 fps, loads the world in about a minute, plays the intro cutscene with lit, textured characters and reaches the prologue with the graphics fully displayed, at about 1 fps. Ray-traced shadows and indirect light are missing. Entering the world reset the display driver in earlier builds; the latest runs, several minutes each, did not.

projects.name: five-star-recomp
projects.tagline: Native recompilation of the Xbox Series release
projects.furthest: The world's lit sky and horizon on screen, surfaces still black, at about a second a frame
projects.status: Its README (read 26 Nov) says the main executable starts under its loader, presents frames to its own window, loads story mode and plays the opening cutscene's art, cards, dialogue and sound at 30 fps. It adds that the world's lit image now reaches the screen, showing the night sky, clouds and the city on the horizon, while surfaces are still black and world frames take about a second each. A commit message of 26 Nov (54f1834) puts world frames at 390 ms. The README also says the game does not run yet. This page counts the world as running, and ranks it at the bottom of stage 6 for a black picture and about 1 fps. All 25,908 shader programs compile. The earlier 18-minute run without a device removal came from a wiki page that is not in this check's sources, so it is dropped. Later commits say a start-up freeze is fixed and that the device is lost after minutes in the world, likely a GPU timeout (9864ac5, 26 Nov). Commit titles of 27 Nov say surface colour and characters are back but the lighting pass still draws nothing (566c05f), and that the driver's shader table fills up before the device loss (e05cbf9). The README itself still says surfaces are black, so the picture lane stays at 1.
projects.source: project README status section (read 27 Nov) and commits 54f1834, 9864ac5, 566c05f and e05cbf9; the README's own wording is that the game does not run yet

picture.note: sky and horizon lit, surfaces black

speed.note: about a second a frame per the README; 390 ms in a commit message

projects.name: Native VIctory for macOS
projects.tagline: Native Apple Silicon port of VIctory, with game code in its own process and GPU work sent straight to Metal; created 26 Nov
projects.furthest: The prologue's world on a Mac, mostly black, at about 0.5 fps on an M5 Pro
projects.status: Its README (27 Nov) says the boot movie, start screen and setup screens run on Metal at about 30 fps, and that the prologue crash is fixed: the game now runs into the prologue's world with the dialogue playing on its test Mac. The picture is mostly black because the compute pass that lights the surfaces is still refused, and the world runs at about 0.5 fps on an M5 Pro with 48 GB, up from 0.07. A cold shader cache can still make the first world frame take over 30 s and trip the game's watchdog, and macOS 15 can hit a Metal compiler crash on a few world pipelines. No session length is given. A branch that recompiles the game to arm64 reaches the intro at 30 fps and is not on main.

projects.name: CGBJ
projects.tagline: Private VIctory/XCL build, reportedly the one briefly public as codec-d/cool_fox. No public code now
projects.furthest: Free roam at an average of 20 fps on NVIDIA, as claimed by its owner (unconfirmed)
projects.status: A report passed to this page says CGBJ was public for a short time as codec-d/cool_fox, was cloned and forked by many people, and is now private again. This page confirmed that the repository returns 404 and that a re-upload of its commits exists (last commit 2026-11-26T06:33Z, a Windows build and NVIDIA shader work), but no source read here ties the name CGBJ to that account, so the link is unconfirmed. The README in that copy carries the VIctory-7900XTX figures, so it is not used for CGBJ's lanes. The owner reportedly rates story progress at 80%, rendering at 0.85 and stability at 0.85, with an average of 20 fps on an NVIDIA card with 10 GB of RAM and 16 GB of VRAM, which the owner says is not a typo. PortWatch, another tracker, is reported to have verified the build; this page has seen neither that check nor the build. The ratings are not measurements with units. Because the 20 fps average is a relayed owner claim with no scene or method, this page leaves the speed lane empty rather than rank the build on it. The picture lane keeps the earlier press reading, since 0.85 does not describe the picture, and no session length is given, so stability is empty.
projects.source: reports passed to this page's editor with the owner's figures, a PortWatch claim and the cool_fox history, 26 Nov; repo codec-d/cool_fox returns 404; commit list of a third-party copy read 26 Nov (not linked); second-hand, identity unconfirmed; earlier press reports

projects.name: Leonida
projects.tagline: The first large recompilation effort. Its repository is gone; Leonida Continued carries on the code with its full history
projects.furthest: The landing prompt, then the story load runs to its end; no world frame yet

Leonida Continued carries on the same code with its full commit history. Its README (25 Nov) says the game boots on native Windows and on Linux through Proton, shows the launch movie, the first-run pages and the landing prompt, which respond to a pad, then runs the story load to its end and enters the world phase. No world frame has been verified on any test machine yet. All 26,503 of the game's shaders translate to SPIR-V and pass validation.

projects.name: OpenScarlett (Community Edition)
projects.tagline: Xbox Series runtime for Windows and Linux
projects.furthest: The start screen after the intro movie, at 30 fps
projects.status: Runs the first-boot settings, legal and start screens at a steady 30 fps and plays the 4K intro movie with sound, then stops while it streams in the scene behind the menus, according to its README. About nine in ten of the game's shaders translate. Commits on 25 Nov describe fixes found in a newer title's first scene. e6b7abc says that scene ran to its 228-second test limit without a GPU reset. e043ba4 says its world was still empty, with every G-buffer target black, and describes a shader fix it had not yet verified. The README does not say the scene is shown, so the stage is unchanged.
projects.source: project README (it calls the game "a newer retail game") and commits 1b7c40d, c1751e2, e6b7abc and e043ba4 (25 Nov)

projects.name: Xbox2Windows
projects.tagline: Static recompiler and runtime for Xbox Series executables
projects.furthest: The intro, the setup text and a loading screen (modified build)
projects.status: A modified diagnostic build, which skips failed checks automatically, played the intro, showed readable setup text and reached loading on an RTX 4060 laptop. Starting the original executable is not yet shown. Its README now says a DXIL route exists for 26,500 of the 26,503 shader records.
projects.source: project README (re-read 26 Nov; claims unchanged) and its progress issue

projects.name: g6shim
projects.tagline: Stand-in system libraries for the Series release
projects.furthest: The account picker, at about 12 fps
projects.status: Starts the game, opens all its archives and renders its screens up to the account picker at about 12 frames a second. About 84% of the game's shaders translate. A commit on 24 Nov adds an offline console with one signed-in user, the README's next step, but no new screen is reported yet. A later commit adds options to size the window or cover the monitor.
projects.source: project README (it names the game by its title ID, 7952987A) and commits 9f5bd4f and 7255852

projects.name: TuxBox
projects.tagline: Runs Xbox Series games on Linux through Proton
projects.furthest: The prologue cutscene on Linux, held back by memory limits
projects.status: Its README (27 Nov) says no retail game is playable yet and lists GTA VI on Linux as reaching the prologue cutscene, currently fighting memory limitations, and untested on Windows. Games are tested on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. It gives no frame rate and does not claim the world, so this page keeps stage 5. It is the furthest Linux-first project.
projects.source: project README (27 Nov) and its recent merged pull requests

projects.name: GTA6-BootTest
projects.tagline: Boot harness with stand-in libraries and its own shader translator
projects.furthest: The prompt bar of the start screen; the screens after it are black
projects.status: Boots, streams its archives, runs the frame loop and draws its first interface screen, the start-screen prompt bar, through translated shaders. Screens after that go black again.
projects.source: project README

projects.name: OpenScarlett
projects.tagline: Xbox Series runtime; plays Minecraft's Series build at 60 fps
projects.furthest: The game's 4K interface and a full-colour video render, according to its commits
projects.status: Commit ef763eb says GTA VI finishes all 249 of its start-up tasks and runs its interface loop at 30 fps. Two later commits that day report the retail title's interface rendering at 3840 by 2160 on a GTX 1650 Ti (f8e24d4) and full-colour 4K video playback (c382f68). A newer commit (022a8b2, 24 Nov) mentions 'RAGE9' rendering at 720p and 4K and a locked 30 fps landing screen. None says which screens were reached, so it ranks last in stage 5.
projects.source: commits ef763eb, f8e24d4, c382f68 and 022a8b2 (24 Nov); the README does not cover the game yet

projects.name: palmetto
projects.tagline: Solo clean-room runtime, started from Leonida's work
projects.furthest: A window shows presented frames, all black
projects.status: Per its commits, the game's present call goes to a real window and draws execute without a hang. A 300-second boot presented about 33,300 frames, all pure black. A 1,200-second boot (f5596dc, 25 Nov) shows the same black frames and a repeating two-pass blit loop with no new content. Later commits (to 58a6036, 25 Nov) say the loader is never re-armed after start-up, and that adding audio imports, a DirectStorage shim and a pipeline cache left every capture black and the loading state unmoved. One of them cuts graphics pipeline creation on a warm boot from 14.7 to 3.9 s. The README still describes the older state. Commits of 26 Nov (87ca21f to f6dcbd2) say a mitigation stops the boot from dying at its third stage, but the boot then waits there for a loading job that never finishes, the movie player has no buffers and every capture is still black.
projects.source: commits 523d947 to f6dcbd2 (24 to 26 Nov), measured on an RTX 4090

projects.name: xbox-emulator
projects.tagline: General Xbox Series runtime, a continuation of TomBox
projects.furthest: Six minutes of presented frames, all black (contributor's branch)
projects.status: A contributor reports running the game on an experimental branch for six minutes, with at least 900 frames presented at up to about 5 a second. Every frame sampled was fully black, so no screen of the game has been seen. The project's own README still lists the game as not run.
projects.source: open PR #371 by a contributor, not merged; GTX 1070 Ti

projects.name: Holy-Interoperability
projects.tagline: Compatibility layer for Xbox Series games
projects.furthest: One frame presented, then the game stops in its start-up code
projects.status: A retail title it does not name loads, creates its graphics device, streams its start-up data and presents its first frame after about 30 seconds, then stops in its own start-up code. The README says nothing it draws has been seen yet.
projects.source: project README

also_watched.name: Leonida CE
also_watched.note: Was ranked at stage 4. On 25 Nov its main branch was rebased onto VIctory's code and its README now carries VIctory's own status text below a short note, with no measurement of its own, so it is not ranked. Its older runtime, which its README says reaches the legal terms screen, is kept on a legacy branch.

also_watched.name: Project ReCity
also_watched.note: Static recompilation toolchain with a Vulkan renderer. Its README says the game does not boot yet (status pre-boot), so it is not ranked.

also_watched.name: VIctory-macOS
also_watched.note: Brings VIctory to Apple Silicon Macs through Wine. Its README (27 Nov) says the game reaches the world on several Macs and stays there, in one case for over 20 minutes, at 0.4 to 3.4 seconds a frame with the scene mostly black, and that nobody has reached gameplay. It is not ranked while its figures come from tester reports.

also_watched.name: VIPort (formerly VIctory V2)
also_watched.note: Renamed from VIctory V2. An integration fork of VIctory that merged open community pull requests in batches; its README says it has not merged from upstream since 25 Nov. Its status text repeats VIctory's own figures (world at 1 to 2 seconds a frame, unlit) and gives no measurement of its own, so it is not ranked.

also_watched.name: Leonida Legacy (ProjectLeonidaL)
also_watched.note: On 25 Nov this repository replaced its Leonida code with Leonida Legacy, a renamed copy of the victory-fork code. Its README says its world frame rates are victory-fork's and have not been measured again on its own machine, so it is not ranked.

also_watched.name: G6Recomp
also_watched.note: Static recompiler. The loader and boot milestones are in progress, and a first frame is not started.

also_watched.name: cool_fox (DoubleGhosty)
also_watched.note: Created 26 Nov and described as a continuation of the cool_fox runtime. Its README lists merged fixes from VIctory-7900XTX, DexNom, Belobug and others and gives no measurement of its own, so it is not ranked.

forecast.definition: At least one project shows 30 minutes or more in the game world under player control, at 20 frames a second or better on some PC, without a crash.
rests_on: The executable surfaced on 23 November. Three days later a dozen or more public projects report the game world running, KLBF Lab reports finishing the first mission and reaching free roam, and Vice-Tay reports a boat mission section played by hand. Two private builds, CGBJ and one shown on a Rumble stream, are said to be in the world too, but both rest on reports this page has not confirmed.

Other games show the pace. XCL's repository opened on the evening of 20 November, and by the evening of 22 November it listed two smaller retail games, Minecraft Preview and Unicorn Overlord, as fully playable. No project has done this with a game the size of GTA VI.

The picture is arriving. KLBF Lab (a fix for dark faces in shade in its newest test build) and ScarlettPort (lit rooms without ray tracing since engine 0.4.6) light shaded places with stand-ins or fixes of their own; others still show anything out of the sun as black, because no build runs the game's ray-traced lighting properly yet.

Speed is the long pole. VIctory took 0.5 to 1.8 seconds per world frame on 23 November. On 25 November AnyXboxX's maintainer measured a median of 13.8 fps in the open world after moving to a new code base (about 12.5 earlier that day, about 5 before it), in 13-minute runs; that is one machine and self-reported. On 26 November KLBF Lab reported an average of 14.0 fps (median 14.5) over a session still running at 37 minutes, Kelvaroq reports about 10 fps over a 36-minute outside session, victory-fork 8 to 14 with sessions of up to 49 minutes that ended in a device loss, and Flamingo 9 to 10 at the first boat mission. VIctory-7900XTX reports 16 to 20 fps with ray tracing off in one street scene, with no session length. Vice-Tay's README reports a median of 21.1 fps over 30 minutes played by hand on an RTX 4090 with the Series S profile, the first report here that reaches 20 fps and 30 minutes together. This page treats it with caution: it is one self-reported session, the README does not say how it ended and the picture has listed faults. On 27 November AnyXboxX, which now builds on Vice-Tay's code, reported a median of about 24 fps at 1080p over a 14-minute session on an RTX 4070 SUPER, so two separate machines now report 20 fps or more, though only Vice-Tay's session reaches 30 minutes. A private build on a stream is said to show 12 to 15, unconfirmed. Playable needs 20 for 30 minutes without a crash.

Where the time goes is now measured, and it is not mostly the graphics card. rorodev6's build spends 22 to 40 ms of a 113 to 141 ms frame on GPU work and the rest copying the game's memory to and from the card, on one thread. victory-fork finds its submit thread and the card both close to full, and cutting one alone moved the frame by 0 to 7%. Getting to 20 fps means removing most of that copying, which is deeper work than the gains of the first two days.

The playable bar does not require correct lighting, only 20 frames a second for 30 minutes. A build could skip the ray-traced passes to get there. Stability has moved: KLBF Lab reports a 77-minute session on a test build that the testers ended themselves, Kelvaroq an outside tester's 36 minutes at about 10 fps, and Vice-Tay a 30-minute session at 21.1 fps. If a second run or an outside tester confirms Vice-Tay, or says it ended without a crash, the page would call it playable.

Work is shared across projects. victory-fork, AnyXboxX, Kelvaroq and ScarlettPort build on VIctory, and fixes move between XCL and the VIctory family within days. AnyXboxX's jump came from taking in a bundle of those fixes at once, which is the kind of gain that can repeat.

Takedowns are now on the record. On 24 November GitHub published a Take-Two notice against Leonida and applied it to its whole network of 3,007 repositories. The notice argues that requiring the game files, given when the project appeared and what it targets, points to the leaked copy. That argument would fit most projects listed here, though none has been named so far. A notice cannot stop private builds, but it could break up the open work the public projects depend on. On 25 November two more ranked repositories, ztrx and victory-perf, disappeared; no source says why.

chances.label: Stalls until an official PC release

milestones.label: 10 fps in free roam
milestones.value: reached Wed 25 Nov, self-reported (AnyXboxX, median 13.8 fps in the open world)

milestones.label: 20 fps over a 30-minute session
milestones.value: reported Thu 26 Nov by Vice-Tay (median 21.1 fps, one session, self-reported, ending not stated); AnyXboxX reported about 24 fps over 14 minutes on Fri 27 Nov

forecast.revision_note: Moved forward from Tue 1 Dec to Mon 30 Nov. This check adds evidence on speed, the gap the earlier move rested on: AnyXboxX's maintainer measured a median of about 12.5 fps in the open world after switching code base, up from about 5 earlier the same day, and Kelvaroq reports about 10 fps over a 36-minute outside session. Both are self-reported on one machine each, and no project shows 20 fps and 30 minutes together, so the move is one day, not more. A private build said to run 12 to 15 fps on a stream is unconfirmed and was not used. Takedown risk is unchanged. The chance by Sun 29 Nov rises from 3 in 10 to 4 in 10.

updates.title: AnyXboxX reports 24 fps in Full HD and moves to second; Native VIctory for macOS reaches the world
points: AnyXboxX's README now reports a median of about 24 fps over a 14-minute session at 1080p on an RTX 4070 SUPER, after moving onto Vice-Tay's code, with about 20 fps at 4K. Speed now meets the bar, its stability lane (14 minutes, ending not stated) is one step short, and it moves to second.
Native VIctory for macOS enters stage 6: its README says the prologue crash is fixed and the world runs on a Mac at about 0.5 fps with a mostly black picture.

victory-perf is back after being listed as gone, with its README's 4.5 to 14 fps on an RTX 4070 SUPER. victory-fork now reports ray-traced shadows with its structure builder on, at 0.2 to 3 fps. ScarlettPort's README gives 3.4 fps on its own RTX 3060 and quotes community reports of up to 22 fps, which this page treats as second-hand.
The forecast holds at Mon 30 Nov. Two machines now report 20 fps or more, but only Vice-Tay's session reaches 30 minutes, neither says how it ended and neither is confirmed by a second source.

updates.title: Vice-Tay reports 21.1 fps over 30 minutes and tops stage 6; Native VIctory for macOS joins
points: Vice-Tay, a VIctory tree tuned on one RTX 4090, is new on the page: its README reports 30 minutes in the world played by hand at a median of 21.1 fps, from the prison through the boat section to an island. Speed and length both reach the bar's numbers, so it ranks first at stage 6. It stays at stage 6 because it is one self-reported session, the README does not say how it ended and the picture still has listed faults.

AnyXboxX's README now says 16 to 17 fps, but a later commit restores the base that measured a median of 14.2, so this page uses 14.2. The 13-minute and 23-minute sessions it cited before are not in the sources, so its stability lane is empty and it moves below Kelvaroq.

VIctory-7900XTX rewrote its figures again: 16 to 20 fps on the Series X profile with ray tracing off, and 9 to 10 with it on. VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README now carries the older text of that project, so it moves up on a 19 fps figure of unclear provenance. ScarlettPort's rebuilt renderer gives a fuller picture at about 3 fps on an RTX 3060.

Native VIctory for macOS joins at stage 5: story mode loads on a Mac and the prologue starts, then crashes a few seconds in. palmetto's boot no longer dies at its third stage but still shows only black frames.
The forecast holds at Mon 30 Nov: Vice-Tay's session lacks a stated crash-free finish and no second source confirms it, and no other project moved above 20 fps in a measured run.

updates.title: KLBF Lab reports 14 fps over 37 minutes and takes the lead; five-star-recomp enters stage 6
points: KLBF Lab's README reports a new test build whose session, still running at 37 minutes without a crash, averaged 14.0 fps (median 14.5) on one RX 9070 XT. With its earlier 77-minute session it is one step short of the playable bar on speed, and it moves above AnyXboxX.

victory-fork's README now reports 8 to 9.5 fps at the first boat mission and 10 to 14 in lighter views, with the card still lost 30 to 50 minutes in. It moves to second, level with KLBF Lab on steps short and behind it on picture.

VIctory-7900XTX rewrote its README: it now gives one city street at about 19 to 22 fps with optional patches on, and no session length, so its stability lane is empty and it ranks lower. Flamingo's README no longer reports 14 fps or a 15-minute run, and gives 9 to 10 fps in the boat cutscene.
five-star-recomp's README now says the world's lit image reaches the screen at about a second a frame with black surfaces, so it moves from stage 5 to the bottom of stage 6.
The forecast holds at Mon 30 Nov: speed on a long session moved from about 13.8 to 14 fps and no project shows 20 fps for 30 minutes.

updates.title: CGBJ reported to have been public briefly as cool_fox
points: A report says CGBJ was public for a short time as codec-d/cool_fox, widely cloned and forked, and is private again; the repository now returns 404.
A copy of that repository's history shows commits by codec_d up to 2026-11-26T06:33Z, so work is likely still going on, but this page could not confirm that CGBJ and codec_d are the same project.
CGBJ's stage, lanes and rank are unchanged: no first-hand figures for it were available to read.

updates.title: VIctory-7900XTX added; CGBJ owner reports 20 fps
points: VIctory-7900XTX, a VIctory-based build for the RX 7900 XTX, is new on the page: its README reports 19 to 22 fps in the first boat mission and a 41-minute session without a crash, with 6 to 10 fps in a street chase.

CGBJ's owner reportedly claims an average of 20 fps on an NVIDIA card, story progress at 80% and PortWatch verification; this page has seen neither the build nor the check, so the figures are marked unconfirmed and kept out of its ranking lanes.
The VIctory-Belobug-AMD README now carries the same text and figures as VIctory-7900XTX, which explains the provenance question noted earlier.

updates.title: AnyXboxX reports 13.8 fps; victory-fork logs 49-minute sessions
points: AnyXboxX's README now gives a median of 13.8 fps in the open world in automated 13-minute runs, up from about 12.5, with no crash; its longest session with a stated length is still the 23-minute Linux run.
victory-fork's README reports 9 to 12 fps in rooms and four sessions of 6, 49, 31 and 38 minutes, each ended by a lost graphics card, so it now meets the 30-minute bar on stability.

VIctory-Belobug-AMD's default branch now carries a README for an RX 7900 XTX fork with a clone address under another account; this page cannot tell whose measurements these are and ranks it on the lowest reading.
five-star-recomp's status wiki says its lit world now shows a night sky and a world frame takes about 969 ms; it stays at stage 5 because the README and the wiki disagree on whether the world runs.

updates.title: AnyXboxX reports about 12.5 fps and takes the lead; Kelvaroq and a stream build join
points: AnyXboxX's README says its maintainer measured a median of about 12.5 fps in the open world on an RTX 4070 SUPER after moving to a new code base, up from about 5. Its longest measured session is still the 23-minute Linux run, so it leads stage 6 by picture and frame rate, two steps short of the playable bar.

Kelvaroq, opened on 24 Nov, joins fourth, level with the leaders on steps short: its README reports the prologue at about 10 fps and an outside tester's 36-minute session without a crash. It calls itself playable; this page's 20 fps bar is not met, and its picture lane is empty.

A private build shown on darkworldhm's Rumble stream is added as unverified: reported at 12 to 15 fps in free roam, swinging 5 to 24, with no crash so far. Code is not public and this page has not seen it, and no session length is given, so its stability lane is empty and it ranks sixth in stage 6, below victory-fork.

victory-fork's README reports a water read-back switch that gets a boat mission past its sinking point, in a run that then lost the device. Leonida CE moves to the watch list because its main branch is now VIctory's code with no measurement of its own.
The forecast moves from Tue 1 Dec to Mon 30 Nov, because the best open-world frame rate on this page rose from about 7 to about 12.5 in one day.

updates.title: victory-fork moves up on a higher frame rate
points: victory-fork's README now gives about 8 to 10 fps in the first rooms and 5 to 8.5 in the opening cutscene, on one RTX 4070. Its speed meter rises a step, and it moves above AnyXboxX to third in stage 6.
The ProjectLeonidaL repository now holds Leonida Legacy, a renamed copy of the victory-fork code with no measurements of its own. It stays on the watch list.
The forecast holds at Tue 1 Dec: no project reports a speed gain in free roam since the last check.

updates.title: Forecast moves to Tue 1 Dec; victory-perf's repository is gone
points: victory-perf's repository now returns 404, so it is marked gone with empty lanes. Its figures of up to 14 fps were its own, from one machine, and were never confirmed.

PortWatch, another tracker, pinned a note at about 18:57 UTC saying it has found no evidence of any build above 10 fps in free roam. No project on this page reports more than that in free roam; Flamingo's 9 to 14 fps is indoors in the first scene, self-reported, and stays marked unconfirmed.
victory (rorodev6) joins at stage 6: its README reports the opening cutscene and the prologue at 7 to 9 fps on one RX 6700 XT.

The forecast moves from Sun 29 Nov to Tue 1 Dec, and the chance by Sun 29 Nov falls to 3 in 10: stability looks solved, but free-roam speed is still under 10 fps and most of each frame goes to memory copies.

updates.title: Leonida returns to the standings at stage 5
points: Leonida, the first large recompilation effort, is back in the ranking at stage 5, marked as gone because its original repository no longer exists. Its entry follows Leonida Continued, which keeps the full history.

Leonida Continued's README now says the game shows its launch movie, first-run pages and landing prompt on Windows and Linux, then finishes the story load. No world frame is verified yet, so it ranks second in stage 5, behind five-star-recomp.
The forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: In-game projects are now read on picture, speed and stability
points: Every stage-6 project is now read on three lanes, picture, speed and stability, and stage 6 is ordered by them. KLBF Lab leads, 2 steps short of the playable bar: its README reports 77 minutes without a crash on a test build, but 5 to 9 fps.

Flamingo is second, also 2 steps short, at 9 to 14 fps with 15-minute runs. AnyXboxX adds a 23-minute Linux run at a median 3.7 fps, and VIctory's README now reaches the prologue, fully drawn, at about 1 fps.
VIctory-Belobug-AMD now reports 5 to 7 fps, up from 3 to 5. ztrx's repository returns 404, so its entry can no longer be checked and its lanes are empty.
The forecast date is unchanged; its reasons now reflect the 77-minute session and the faster frame rates.

updates.title: Flamingo and DexNom Runtime join at stage 6
points: Flamingo joins above victory-fork: its README reports the first gameplay scene under player control at about 14 fps on one RTX 4070, and 9 to 12 fps looking into the room.
DexNom Runtime, a Radeon-focused fork of VIctory, joins low in stage 6: its test report reaches the outdoor City scene from a save at about 1 fps with experimental ray tracing on an RX 7900 XTX.
KLBF Lab's README now says a test build fixes the boat in the first mission, with seaplane take-off and flight working. Neither new project meets the 20 fps bar, so the forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: Four projects join at stage 6; KLBF Lab takes the lead
points: KLBF Lab joins at the top of stage 6: its README reports play from the prison prologue into the first mission after it, up to a seaplane, at about 5 to 7 fps on one RX 9070 XT, with 74 minutes in one session without a crash.

ztrx joins with the prologue played from the cell to the boat chase at 1 to 3 fps on an RTX 3050, and victory-perf with 9 to 14 fps in prologue interiors on an RTX 4070 SUPER. VItoriaBr reports the open world at up to 6 fps on an RTX 5060 Ti.

victory-fork stays below AnyXboxX, KLBF Lab, ztrx and victory-perf: its own README describes the first rooms, 2.5 to 7 fps, and says it is not playable. None of the new projects meets the 20 fps bar, and the forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: victory-fork reports 7 to 8 fps in the first rooms; an AMD fork joins
points: victory-fork's newest commit message reports 7 to 8 fps in the first rooms and 10 to 12 in lighter views on an RTX 4070, one run. It also says a first play session past the first rooms lost the device in the open world. The 20 fps bar is not met.
VIctory-Belobug-AMD, a VIctory fork for Radeon cards created on 25 Nov, joins at stage 6: its README says the lit world renders at 3 to 5 fps on an RX 9070 XT.
ScarlettPort's v0.2.1 fixes its tile-grid overlay and stays at about 4 fps. TuxBox's README says its story intro still stalls, and palmetto's frames are still black after its newest commits.
VIctory V2 is now VIPort, and VIctory-macOS reports the world on two Macs at 0.1 to 0.2 fps. The forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: PercyScarlett reaches the opening prison scene; victory-fork reports 6 to 7 fps with switches on
points: PercyScarlett's v1.0 README says the game reaches the opening prison scene, lit and textured, at about 2 to 3 fps on an RTX 2060 SUPER. It moves from stage 5 to stage 6.
victory-fork's README reports the first room at 6 to 7 fps on an RTX 4070 with all its new switches on; the defaults give about 4.5 to 5. The 20 fps bar is not met.
ScarlettPort reports about 4 fps in the prologue and has synced its runtime copy to victory-fork. palmetto's newest commit says its loader is never re-armed, and it stays at stage 4.
OpenScarlett (Community Edition) has a commit saying a newer title's world was still empty, so it stays at stage 5. The forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: victory-fork renders the first room; five-star-recomp draws the cutscene world offscreen
points: victory-fork's README now says the first room renders with walls, textures, people and lamps at 190 to 450 ms a frame, and its newest commit says the graphics card is now the limit at 250 to 380 ms.
five-star-recomp's README says the opening cutscene's 3D world now draws into the G-buffer, but lighting and composition do not reach the screen. It stays at stage 5.
TuxBox and OpenScarlett (Community Edition) have commits that point toward a loaded world or scene. Neither README claims it, so both stay at stage 5.
VIctory V2, a fork that merges VIctory's open pull requests, joins the watch list. No stage or forecast changed.

updates.title: AnyXboxX reports two missions played; XCL enters its 3D world
points: AnyXboxX's README now reports 4.8 to 5.4 fps in the world and, second-hand, a contributor playing about 45 minutes at about 2 fps and finishing the first two missions. It moves to the top of stage 6; the 20 fps bar is not met.
XCL's README says that on an unmerged integration branch the game reaches its 3D world at 5 to 6 fps, with an incomplete picture. XCL moves from stage 5 to stage 6.
Leonida CE moves from stage 3 to stage 4: its README reports 10+ minutes without a crash, with black frames presented. palmetto's 1,200-second run is still black.
Palmwave's repository now returns 404 and is marked gone. five-star-recomp's README now gives 30 fps for its cutscene art, and TuxBox reports the story intro on Linux. The forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: Palmwave draws the world; five-star-recomp starts the opening cutscene
points: Palmwave's README now says the world's street, trees, people and a car reach the game's G-buffer, at 2 to 5 seconds a frame. The picture the game presents is still almost one dark colour.
five-star-recomp says its story load finishes and the opening cutscene starts, at under 2 frames a second. It stays at stage 5.
victory-gta6 has been renamed victory-fork, and AnyXboxX now pins a commit with the device-loss fix. ScarlettPort shows the world under stand-in lighting at about 1 fps.
palmetto's 300-second run presented about 33,300 frames, all black, and no stage changed. The forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: five-star-recomp's story load holds for 300 seconds
points: five-star-recomp's status files now say the story load runs 300 seconds without a fault, but it does not finish. It stays at stage 5.
palmetto's newest commit rules out culling, depth clipping and its pipeline stand-ins as the cause of its black frames. It stays at stage 4.
g6shim added window-size options. Its furthest screen is unchanged, and the forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: Entries re-checked against every README; ScarlettPort added
points: Every entry was compared with its project's current README and recent commits. victory-gta6 now reports no device loss in normal runs after a fix, and AnyXboxX merged PR #167 and shows the 3D picture at about 4 fps.
ScarlettPort, started on 24 Nov, joins at stage 6: it reaches the movement tutorial at about 1 fps, with a black picture.

palmetto moves to stage 4: its commits report a window with presented frames and executing draws, still all black. The californiaAlmonds OpenScarlett moves to stage 5, on commits reporting the game's 4K interface and video.
Leonida CE joins at stage 3 with a modified build, and a second Leonida continuation is now watched. The forecast is unchanged.

updates.title: Forecast moves to Sun 29 Nov; Take-Two notice published
points: The forecast for a playable build moves from Tue 1 Dec to Sun 29 Nov. Frame rate roughly tripled in a day, XCL showed two smaller retail games going from a new repository to playable in about two days, and the playable bar does not need ray-traced lighting.
GitHub published a Take-Two takedown notice against Leonida on 24 November and applied it to all 3,007 repositories in its network. No other project on this page is named in it.
No project changed stage in this check.

updates.title: Rankings rechecked; victory-gta6 takes the lead
points: Every project was rechecked against its own README, commits and pull requests. victory-gta6, a fork of VIctory, is added at the top of stage 6 with a lit first gameplay scene at 2 to 4 frames a second.
AnyXboxX's maintainer reports about 13 minutes of player-controlled play at about 4 frames a second on that fork, in an open pull request. The 30-minute, 20 fps bar for playable is not met.
g6shim moves from stage 2 to stage 5: its README shows it reaching the account picker at about 12 frames a second. The entry here was out of date.
xbox-emulator joins at stage 4 from a contributor's black-frame run. Leonida leaves the ranking because its continuation, which keeps its full history, says the game never booted under it.

updates.title: palmetto builds every pipeline; XCL moves house
points: palmetto now builds all 10,241 of the game's graphics pipelines and records about 42,700 draws per run. None executes yet, so it stays at stage 3.
XCL's repository has moved from ivall/xcl to xcl-dev/xcl. Links on this page now point to the new home.
No project changed stage in this check.

updates.title: Tracker goes live with 16 projects
points: Sixteen projects are ranked from their own READMEs, plus four on the watch list and four general Xbox layers with no GTA VI claims.
Three public projects report the game world running: AnyXboxX, VIctory and Palmwave. None has a usable picture yet.
The first forecast puts playable around Tue 1 Dec, with speed as the main obstacle.

method.label: Playable builds
method.text: None exist. Anything offered as a playable download of GTA VI for PC is fake, and fakes have carried malware.

method.label: What the projects use
method.text: They work from a leaked Xbox Series build. Rockstar has not announced a PC version. This page does not link to the leak or explain how to get or run it.

method.label: Sources
method.text: Each project's public repository: its README, status files, commits and pull requests. Press reports where a project has no public code. Every row names its source.

method.label: Claims
method.text: Stages are what each project says about itself, unless the source line says otherwise. This page does not run the code, and most claims are unverified.

method.label: Ranking
method.text: By stage first. In-game projects, at stage 6, are then ordered by their three lanes, explained below the stages. In the other stages, by the furthest point each project has reached in the game's own sequence of screens, furthest first; when two are at about the same point, the one with a measured frame rate, an unmodified build or a public, first-hand source ranks higher. An equals sign marks a tie that none of these separates.

method.label: Who writes it
method.text: An AI assistant (Claude) checks the repositories when asked and rewrites the entries. It can be wrong; the source links are there to check it.

method.label: Affiliation
method.text: None. Not connected to Rockstar Games, Take-Two Interactive, Microsoft or any project listed. Names link to repositories to credit the work.

lanes_intro: A project that is in-game, at stage 6, is also read on three lanes. Each step is this page's reading of what the project reports about itself, or of the source its row names, and an empty meter means no figure is reported. Blue marks the steps that meet the playable bar: 20 frames a second and 30 minutes without a crash.
lanes_order: Rows at that stage are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session.

lanes.name: Picture
lanes.about: What the project says is on screen in the game's world.

steps.label: Lit where the sun falls, shadows black or dark
Lit in light and shade, with visible faults
Lit and whole, small faults only
The console's picture, ray tracing included

lanes.name: Speed
lanes.about: The middle of the frame rates it reports in play, in rendered frames a second (fps).

steps.label: 30 fps or more, the console's rate

lanes.name: Stability
lanes.about: The longest session it reports without a crash.
